newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras in talks with Venezuela's PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras in talks with Venezuela's PDVSA.

text.p: The presidents of Brazil state oil monopoly Petrobras and Venezuela state oil firm PDVSA agreed to establish by July the areas of Venezualan oil and gas exploration and production in which Petrobras can participate, Petrobras said in a statement.

The Brazilian oil giant would take part via its Braspetro subsidiary, responsible for operations outside of Brazil, which may set up a company financed with Petrobras and PDVSA capital, the statement said.
Braspetro Vice-President Jose Coutinho Barbosa will be heading a delegation traveling to Caracas in June to negotiate the partnership.
Petrobras President Joel Renno and his PDVSA counterpart Luis Guisti also agreed to continue talks on how to increase Brazil's imports of Venezuelan oil and petroleum products.
The aim is to increase oil imports from Venezuela to 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) to make it Brazil's second biggest supplier of oil after Argentina with 142,000 bpd, Petrobras said.
Venezuela is currently the third largest supplier with around 120,000 bpd after Saudi Arabia with 123,000 bpd.

The company presidents also approved an agenda to deepen negotiations under Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's program for greater integration in the Latin American energy sector. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
